metadata.note: The Rochester and State Line Railroad, the line that put Rochester on a railroad of its own to the Pennsylvania coalfields, and the ancestor of the Rochester half of the Buffalo, Rochester and Pittsburgh. Chartered Oct 6 1869 with a ceremonial groundbreaking Aug 21 1872, it opened to Le Roy in 1874, reached Warsaw in June 1877 and Salamanca on May 16 1878 -- 108 miles. Its charter had described a route down the Genesee through Caledonia, Portageville, Belfast and Wellsville, but as built the line was shifted west through Warsaw and Ellicottville to reach Salamanca, where its standard gauge met the Atlantic and Great Western's 6-foot broad gauge and cars were moved between the two on the Ramsey transfer device. It never earned enough to service its debt: William H. Vanderbilt held most of the stock by 1879, foreclosure began Feb 6 1880, and after a syndicate bought the equity for $600,000 the Rochester and Pittsburgh Railroad replaced it on Jan 29 1881. That company failed in turn, and Adrian Iselin's 1885 purchase split it into the Pittsburgh and State Line Railroad in Pennsylvania and the Buffalo, Rochester and Pittsburgh in New York, under which this became the BR&P's Rochester Division -- the eastern leg of the Y that met the Buffalo leg at Ashford Junction and ran on to Salamanca. This layer fills in that Rochester leg, which buffalo_rochester_pittsburgh_railway.geojson did not cover: that file traces only the Buffalo-Punxsutawney-Pittsburgh line. Era boundaries follow real, sourced milestones; headway_min and avg_speed_kmh are estimates, not from timetables.

metadata.not_yet_sourced: No per-station mileposts were found for this line, so the traced geometry is checked against crow-flight distance leg by leg and against the documented 108-mile total, not against booked mileage the way the Lehigh Valley and Atlantic & Great Western layers are. Timetable frequencies and speeds for every era are estimates. Also not drawn here: the Silver Lake Branch (Silver Lake Junction - Silver Springs - Silver Lake - Perry), the exact location of Ashford Junction, and the dates individual segments were abandoned.
geometry_sources: OpenStreetMap via Overpass API, shortest-path search over the OSM rail graph between Rochester, Chili, Le Roy, Pavilion, Warsaw, Bliss, Arcade, Machias, Ellicottville and Salamanca. Routed in three passes -- preferring live rail, preferring abandoned corridors, and preferring abandoned corridors with a wide gap stitch for grades OSM has broken into disconnected pieces -- and the best result per leg was kept.

Result: 7 of 9 legs followed real track, giving 183 km against the documented 108 miles (174 km), about 5% over -- the normal margin for traced track against a booked figure. Straight-line approximations remain on: XX Chili -> Le Roy: rail 37km (1.64x); abandoned 38km (1.67x); stitched 38km (1.67x) -- STRAIGHT LINE used | XX Bliss -> Arcade: rail 50km (3.39x); abandoned 50km (3.40x); stitched 50km (3.40x) -- STRAIGHT LINE used

Per-leg tracing result: ok Rochester -> Chili: 10 pts, 18km vs 14km crow (1.32x) [rail] | XX Chili -> Le Roy: rail 37km (1.64x); abandoned 38km (1.67x); stitched 38km (1.67x) -- STRAIGHT LINE used | ok Le Roy -> Pavilion: 9 pts, 13km vs 10km crow (1.29x) [rail] | ok Pavilion -> Warsaw: 10 pts, 18km vs 18km crow (1.00x) [rail] | ok Warsaw -> Bliss: 27 pts, 30km vs 20km crow (1.50x) [rail] | XX Bliss -> Arcade: rail 50km (3.39x); abandoned 50km (3.40x); stitched 50km (3.40x) -- STRAIGHT LINE used | ok Arcade -> Machias: 13 pts, 19km vs 14km crow (1.32x) [rail] | ok Machias -> Ellicottville: 12 pts, 22km vs 22km crow (1.04x) [rail] | ok Ellicottville -> Salamanca: 17 pts, 22km vs 13km crow (1.60x) [rail]
